role_and_message.evidence: The three source demonstrations remain single-view 3D reconstruction, dense category-instance correspondence and unsupervised texture transfer.

panel_and_object_coverage.evidence: All four vehicle/aircraft photo-reconstruction comparisons, nine bird shapes and three chair-transfer rows remain; source and target chair roles are retained.

labels_math_and_numbers.evidence: Original panel titles and Source textured mesh/Target meshes labels remain. The training header states unpaired category images with known camera poses exactly as the source caption.

connections_and_direction.evidence: All original chair source-to-target arrows remain, and added single-image-to-3D wording explains the first panel without inserting a cross-panel dependency.

visual_encodings.evidence: Bird correspondence colors and chair textures are source pixels; no invented anatomical color key or changed category mapping is supplied. Blue/green/orange framing merely separates demonstrations.

examples_and_data.evidence: Complete original scientific panels preserve all photographs, meshes, correspondence colors, transfers and example pairings without regeneration of evidence.

unsupported_additions.evidence: Dense correspondence across different shapes/articulations and texture transfer across category instances are directly supported by Figure 1 caption and the first two pages' deformation-field description.

complete_visible_content.evidence: All original data and labels plus the new source-supported text are visible. Repeated titles and generous whitespace are retained for separate quality judgment.

remaining_limitations: Original examples, content and source resolution remain; new text is limited to original caption/body claims. Layout quality is assessed separately.
caption:
Figure 1. Given an unpaired image collection (with known camera poses) of an object category at training time, our approach learns to: (a)
reconstruct the underlying 3D given only a single image at test time, and (b) model dense 3D correspondences across category instances.
The learned correspondence field is articulation-aware, topologically-aware and inherently captures structural properties of the category,
enabling the task of unsupervised texture transfer. Videos and code at https://shivamduggal4.github.io/tars-3D/
